title: Insurer Program Agreements — Tier Placement, Repair Pricing and Claim Billing Terms
content:
The terms below govern the tier of an agreement under the Insurer Program Agreements, how repairs on the insurer's claims are priced, and the market body labor rate an agreement may carry.

## Clauses

1. **Tier.** The tier is the highest one whose annual volume commitment the insurer commits to.
2. **Labor and materials.** Repairs for the insurer's claims are priced at the tier's body labor rate, refinish labor rate, frame and structural steel labor rate, mechanical and electrical labor rate, aluminum structural labor rate and paint and materials rate.
3. **Parts.** The tier's original-equipment parts discount is taken off original-equipment list prices, and the tier's alternate parts target applies as a parts target.
4. **Market body labor rate.** Where the tier permits a market rate, a market body labor rate set on the agreement replaces the tier's body labor rate for every repair of the insurer while it is set, and it is changed no more often than every market rate review interval of the tier, in calendar months; nothing else is overridden.
5. **Towing and storage.** The insurer pays at most the tier's towing cap per tow and the tier's storage cap per storage day.
6. **Teardown.** The center may perform the tier's pre-approved teardown hours of disassembly before approval.
7. **Short pays.** Short pays up to the tier's short pay write-off per repair order are written off without dispute.
8. **Scans and deductibles.** Scans are billable where the tier makes scans billable, and the network collects the deductible on the insurer's behalf where the tier provides for deductible collection by the network.

## Setting and clearing a market rate

A market body labor rate is set or cleared on the agreement one rate change at a time; each change records the market body labor rate, and a market rate of 0.00 clears the override. While no market rate is set, the tier's body labor rate applies.

| Market rate permitted by the tier | Market rate set on the agreement | Body labor rate on the insurer's repairs | Other rates |
|---|---|---|---|
| Yes | Yes | The market body labor rate | The tier's rates |
| Yes | No, or cleared with 0.00 | The tier's body labor rate | The tier's rates |

Refinish, frame and structural steel, mechanical and electrical, aluminum structural and paint and materials are never replaced by a market rate.

## Illustration (hypothetical market rate)

A hypothetical agreement whose tier permits a market rate has a market body labor rate of 66.00 set on it. Every repair of that insurer while the rate is set prices body labor at 66.00 an hour; refinish labor and paint and materials on the same repairs stay at the tier's figures. When the market rate is changed to 0.00, the override is cleared and body labor returns to the tier's body labor rate.

## Tier placement read as cases

- An insurer whose commitment meets the Preferred Direct Repair Agreement commitment but not the Premier Direct Repair Agreement commitment is placed on the Preferred tier, the highest tier whose commitment it commits to.
- An insurer whose commitment meets the commitment of every tier up to and including the Enterprise Master Services Agreement is placed on that tier.

## Points of judgement

- **Is a short pay within the write-off figure disputed?** No; short pays up to the figure, per repair order, are written off without dispute.
- **What do the towing and storage caps limit?** What the insurer pays: at most the towing cap for each tow, and at most the storage cap for each storage day.
- **May disassembly begin before the insurer approves?** Up to the tier's pre-approved teardown hours.
